q1_issues.issue: 'those' — an antecedent-less demonstrative plural — is typed as a group of person, but the instruction set's person fallback is for the personal pronoun 'they'; a non-personal pronoun with no supplied kind falls back to thing, so personhood is asserted without the text supplying it.
The subset group inherits the same unlicensed person typing as the superset.
The modifier in 'specific diseases' is dropped entirely — the object is the bare class symbol disease in all four disjuncts, so no atom records 'specific'.

q2_gaps: an anaphoric demonstrative plural with no antecedent ('of those') — the antecedent-less-pronoun rule covers he/she/they/it but not demonstratives, so nothing fixes the member kind of the presupposed superset

an adjectival modifier on a bare-class generic object ('specific diseases') has no attachment site — the bare class symbol carries no modifier, and the distributive route requires a group witness the generic-object rule forbids
direct quotation of the predicate ('claimed to treat ...') — the instruction set has no treatment of quoted material, so the quotation marks are simply consumed
notes: The partitive shape (superset + SubsetOf + Cardinality 149 + un-reduced (Fraction 55 100)) and the control-verb handling of 'claimed to V' (complement events reified with no tense, controller's Agent copied in, Theme link distributed into each narrow-scope Or branch) both follow the instruction set.
